I will keep my full 2.0 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the system I know best and it fits my land, my labor, and my well irrigation. I farm alone and I am already 68, so I will not make the management too complicated. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because on a very small farm I need stable yield and I cannot afford weak stands. I will do moderate fertilizer use instead of chasing the highest possible yield, because I want a crop I can manage steadily with the money and labor I have. For wheat, I will prepare the land with rotary tillage after maize, sow on time, give more nitrogen than phosphorus and potassium, irrigate at the key stages, and spray only when needed for common diseases and insects. For summer maize, I will plant right after wheat harvest, keep the same 2.0 mu, use hybrid seed, apply enough nitrogen to support grain filling, and irrigate a few times through the hot season because I have well water and summer drought can cut yield badly.

I will keep the plan practical and familiar. I will not choose no-tillage this year because on my small plot I prefer a clean seedbed and even emergence. I will also keep pesticide use limited rather than frequent, because I want to control costs and I do not need complicated management on 2.0 mu. My goal is not the maximum experimental yield; my goal is a dependable harvest from both wheat and maize with work I can still handle by myself.
